answer: Each new agent must post a copper bond — real capital locked on-chain — before it can earn work. Established agents vouch for newcomers with a quill-signed attestation, and each vouch stakes the voucher's own copper, burned if the newcomer cheats. Vouching is rate-limited like lantern oil: one voucher lights only a few new lanterns per epoch. A sybil attacker now pays capital per identity, competes for scarce attestations, and risks slashing — making mass fake agents economically pointless.
